name: Tap to Pay (accept contactless payments on the phone)
plain: Turns the phone into a card reader for merchants.
meaning: Lets a business accept taps from cards and wallets with no extra hardware. Reader code is certified by card schemes.

android.permission: NFC; no OS reader API; PSP SDK (Stripe, Adyen, Square) with PCI MPoC attestation
android.prompt_ui: None for users; device must pass SDK and attestation checks
android.api_surface: PSP SDK on NfcAdapter reader mode
android.note: Android has no first party Tap to Pay API; availability set by the PSP.

ios.prompt_ui: Merchant UI with system tap sheet; Apple review of entitlement
ios.note: iOS 18 adds PIN entry; expanded to more countries by 2026.

limits.headline: Can accept tap payments from cards and wallets on the phone, once approved
limits.user_action: A shop owner opens the payment app and asks the customer to tap a card or phone
can: Take a contactless tap from a card, phone or watch
Ask for a PIN when the payment needs one (iPhone, iOS 18 and later)
Turn the phone into a card reader with no extra hardware
cannot: Run without the payment company's certified software and device checks
Use a built in Android reader feature, since Android has none
Work in every country; iPhone support has grown by region
limits.differs: iPhone uses Apple's own feature after Apple approves the app; Android depends on the payment company's kit and its checks.

story.what_it_is: A way to turn a phone into a card reader so a shop can take taps from cards and wallets.

marketing.name: Tap to Pay on iPhone
marketing.pitch: Accept contactless cards, Apple Pay and other wallets with just an iPhone and a payment app. No extra hardware needed.

story.for_you: If you buy from a market stall or a small shop, the seller holds up a phone and you tap your card on it. It feels like a normal card reader, and you never see the seller's app.
story.for_makers: Small businesses skip the cost and hassle of a card reader. Payment companies like Square and Stripe get more sellers on their platform. Apple restricts access so only approved payment providers can use it.

use_cases.example: A food truck owner takes taps from lunch customers on a phone with no card reader in the truck.
A store clerk walks the floor and checks out a shopper at the shelf, so there is no line at the register.
A delivery driver takes a card payment on the doorstep for cash on delivery orders.
A stall at a music festival or farmers market sells items with only a phone.
A taxi driver in a city with many small cabs takes taps in the back seat.
A repair technician finishes a job at a customer's home and gets paid before leaving.
The phone checks that the card is real and shields the card number from the seller's app.

risks: Card data never visible to the app
Fraud if the seller's phone is stolen
story.android_note: Android has no single built in Tap to Pay. Each payment company builds its own, so it depends on which provider and device.
story.ios_note: iPhone XS and later can take taps. iOS 18 added PIN entry so shoppers can type a PIN on the seller's screen.

technical_bounds: Not open for merchants without a PSP and entitlement on iOS

history.change: Tap to Pay on iPhone in the US
PIN on glass and wider rollout
